correctness.rationale: Hausdorff contraction proves K=sum_{n>=0}diag(a,b)^n B2 unique. Its support points give the exact X(t) and deficit Y(t) series. For b>a², summable curvature at vertical yields D~(1-a²/b)x²/2. At b=a² the head-tail index N~log(1/t)/log(1/a) gives X=t(N+O(1)), D=t²(N+O(1))/2, hence the stated x²/log(1/x) constant. For b<a² the variational split of disk coordinates and weighted Cauchy–Schwarz produce explicit two-sided |x|^q bounds, q=log b/log a>2, not a fictitious asymptotic prefactor. Divergent vertical curvature radius gives C² flatness, positive away; evenness and Taylor contradiction rule out C³ precisely within a³≤b≤a². Finite asymptotic tests corroborate only.
